newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cent lower Wednesday in a technical correction to Tuesday's sharp run-up, traders said.
But many traders added they would not be surprised to see prices come in higher, as the market's tone remained firmly on the side of the bulls.
"Sentiment is up," said one trader. "As soon as there's buying, there are no sellers."

Tuesday, New York arabica futures surged as supply concerns continued to fuel keen speculative buying. July jumped to a new lifetime high of 275.00 cents a lb before settling at 274.30 cents, up 17.45 cents. Second-month September closed 11.45 cents higher at 237.50 cents, while the back months rose 0.50 to 6.00.
The July/September spread, a barometer of near-term supplies, ballooned to 36.80 cents from 30.80 at the close on Friday.
On the July charts, traders were eyeing the 280.00-cent level, a 20-year high reached earlier this month on the now-expired May contract. The next upside objective was seen at 291.00 cents.
After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 49,712 60-kg bags as of May 23. There was no coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
Also after the close, the CSCE said it will raise the margin on the September 1997 coffee "C" contract to $6,500, including a $1,500 spot charge, effective today.
London robusta futures were sharply higher early Wednesday, bolstered by speculative and trade buying. LIFFE July soared $76 at the midday break, to $2,178, the day's high.
